you be the …, I’ll be the …

terms.gloss: pretend not to (know, see); hide that one knows
terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; with quasi and the subjunctive, or the accusative and infinitive
evidence: Plaut. Mil. 4.2.2: dissimulābō, hōs quasi nōn videam (Lewis & Short s.v. dissimulō)
Traupman 106: I’ll pretend I don’t know him, dissimulābō mē eum nōvisse
terms.comment: To hide what is so: dissimulābō mē eum nōvisse is “I’ll hide that I know him”, so “I’ll pretend not to know him”. Its opposite is simulāre, to pretend what is not so.

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation; with quasi and the subjunctive
evidence: Ter. Eun. 3.2.8: assimulābō quasi nunc exeam, “will pretend to be just going out” (Lewis & Short s.v. quasi)
Traupman 106: I’ll pretend I’m leaving, assimulābō quasi abeam

terms.grammar: with the accusative of the person: medicum agere, to be the doctor
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Com. 20: Balliōnem illum … cum agit, agit Chaeream
Tac. H. 1.30: etiam cum amīcum imperātōris ageret
terms.comment: Of an actor taking a part, and of anyone acting as someone else (Lewis & Short). Our use extends it to a child’s part in pretend play, after the children’s games in the examples: medicum agere, ducātūs et imperia lūdere.

phrases.english: I’ll pretend I’m just going out.

phrases.latin: sed ita adsimulātōte, quasi ego sim peregrīnus
phrases.english: but make believe that I am a stranger
I’ll be the doctor, and you be the patient.

phrases.latin: At puerī lūdentēs ‘Rēx eris’ ajunt, ‘sī rēctē faciēs.’
phrases.english: But the boys at play say, “You’ll be king if you do it right.”

phrases.latin: quia ferēbātur ducātūs et imperia lūdere
phrases.english: because he was said to play at generals and emperors

phrases.latin: illī inter ipsōs magistrātūs gerunt et praetextam fascēsque ac tribūnal imitantur
phrases.english: among themselves they hold magistracies, and imitate the bordered toga, the rods, and the judge’s platform

phrases.latin: Fingāmus hanc mēnsam esse tabernam: ego vēndam, tū emēs.
phrases.english: Let’s pretend this table is a shop: I’ll sell, and you’ll buy.

phrases.latin: aedificāre casās, plōstellō adjungere mūrīs, lūdere pār inpār, equitāre in harundine longā
phrases.english: building play-houses, harnessing mice to a little cart, playing odds and evens, riding about on a long cane

phrases.latin: Pīrātās agāmus: hic lectus nostra nāvis erit.
phrases.english: Let’s pretend to be pirates: this bed will be our ship.

phrases.latin: Ego rēgem agam; tū mihi pārēbis.
phrases.english: I’ll be the king, and you’ll do as I say.

phrases.latin: Tū dracōnem age; ego tē fugābō.
phrases.english: You be the dragon, and I’ll chase you away.
